Friended starts from posts and conversation prompts rather than events. That can be gentler than walking into a venue cold, because the first interaction happens in writing and the pace is easier to control. The downside is that it doesn't solve the in-person part. If the real issue is the transition from wanting connection to being in a room with people, Friended keeps you online longer than Timeleft does.

## Find your ideal match based on event style

The right choice depends on the kind of night you can sustain. Use the sections below to match each platform to the format that costs you the least energy.

### For matched small-group dinners [...] ### 6Localized events via Nextdoor

Nextdoor is useful when you want local information and the occasional community event. It's not designed as a social matching product, and the event experience is usually loose enough that you still have to read the room and create your own opening. If you want a night that already has a social container around it, Nextdoor will still leave too much up to you.

### 7Friended: avoiding social exhaustion by starting online [...] ### 5Peanut: low-pressure, but mostly one-on-one

Peanut is designed for mothers and people in similar life stages who want to meet others nearby and start conversations. It's warmer and more specific than a general-purpose social app.

Still, Peanut is built around discovery and connection rather than pre-booked, pre-matched events. The planning and follow-through still sit with you once a connection is made.

Small team meetings (2 to 25 participants). These meetings call for reliable audio and video and simple collaboration features like screen sharing, chat, and shared notes.
 Department or company meetings (25 to 250 participants). Larger internal meetings often need stronger host controls and better recording options.
 Large webinars and virtual conferences (250 to 100,000 or more participants). At this scale, registration, attendee management, polling, Q&A, and tighter audience controls become much more important.
 Hybrid events (in-person and virtual attendees together). Hybrid meetings raise the bar for audio quality, room support, captions, recording, and content sharing because the platform has to create a smooth experience for people in the room along with people joining remotely.
